scope: D033 n76 fig-179 and fig-180; short-lived first independent FIG and DISPLAY review
method: Recorded after opening only the two original PNGs, before reading author report, inventory, FigureSpec, SVG, or modern previews. Coordinates below describe source-screen topology, not measured model coordinates.

marks.observation: One solid horizontal shared principal axis, extending beyond both object and image; no scale or numeric ticks.
One vertical thin-lens symbol through O, with outward arrowheads at its top and bottom.
Upright arrow B to A at the left. B lies on the principal axis; A is above it.
Inverted arrow B1 to A1 at the right. B1 lies on the principal axis; A1 is below it. The printed numerals are subscripts, not separate points.
Two marked F positions on the horizontal axis, one between B and O, the other between O and B1. Both are labelled F.
C and D lie on the lens above and below O. C is at A's height; D is at A1's height.
Solid A to C horizontal ray directed right. At C it refracts downward through the right F to A1, then continues down-right beyond A1.
Solid A to O to A1 straight ray directed down-right, continuing beyond A1.
Solid A through the left F to D ray directed down-right. At D it refracts into the solid horizontal D to A1 ray directed right, continuing beyond A1.
The three physical ray paths, lens, axis, object, and image are solid. No dashed virtual back-extension is present.
Visible labels A, B, C, D, O, F, F, A1, B1. No other named source point, numerical distance, grid, screen, or focal plane.

relationships: B, left F, O, right F, and B1 occur in that order on one shared axis.
A, C are at one height; D, A1 are at another height; object/image are vertical to the axis.
A, left F, D are collinear.
C, right F, A1 are collinear.
All three outgoing physical rays meet at A1, giving a real inverted image.
The pictured image is larger than the pictured object; object lies beyond the left focal point.
Focal positions look approximately symmetric about O; no exact source lengths are supplied.
reviewRisks: Do not invent a source point at 2F or add an instructional screen.
Preserve the three ray constructions and subscript image labels.
The same figure may support later algebraic derivation without changing its source topology.

marks.observation: One horizontal solid principal axis with a rightward arrowhead.
One vertical lens through O with outward arrowheads above and below.
S is an asterisk-like point source on the principal axis to the left of O.
S1 is farther left on the same principal axis, marked at the dashed ray's axis intersection. Its numeral is a subscript.
B is the upper lens intersection of the solid segment rising from S.
The solid S to B ray rises rightward. Beyond B it bends into a shallower rising-right line passing through C and continuing to a rightward arrowhead.
The backward continuation of the outgoing B-C ray is dashed from B leftward through S1 and a little beyond S1. It is not a solid physical incoming ray.

A separate solid oblique P-O-C-Q line rises from lower left through O and C to upper right. P and Q label this line near its extensions; it does not originate at S. Its slope resembles the incoming S-B direction.
A dashed vertical support/focal-plane line passes through C and F on the outgoing/right side, extending above C and below the axis.
C is the marked intersection of the outgoing B-C ray, the oblique construction line, and the vertical dashed plane. F is the plane's marked intersection with the axis.
Visible labels S, S1, B, O, P, Q, C, F. No second left F label or object/image arrow is present.

relationships: S1, S, O, F occur in that order on the shared principal axis.
S, B form the physical incoming ray; B, C form the refracted outgoing ray.
S1, B, C are collinear across the dashed backward and solid forward parts.
P-O-C-Q is a separate construction direction; it must not be misrepresented as a second ray emitted by S.
The construction line through O is parallel to incoming S-B, meeting the outgoing focal plane at C.
C is above F and the outgoing focal plane is perpendicular to the principal axis.
The backward extension meets the axis on the incoming side at S1, depicting a virtual image for an inside-focus source.
reviewRisks: Preserve dashed virtual extension and dashed vertical focal-plane support separately from solid physical rays.
Do not invent a source point for a second physical ray through O.
Verify that P and Q retain construction-line meaning and that C remains on the outgoing plane, not on the lens.
Source arrowhead detail on the oblique construction line is not confidently resolved at original size; do not infer physical light solely from it.

modernAdditionsPolicy: Exact focal normalization, hidden model points, extra arrow markers, and semantic styling may be justified separately, but cannot be claimed as source pixel facts.
